Canonical SHA-256: 76578dea621e1909fe5f8cb755d16e2a32f649a2c5635158c801b5e675485c19. 193 whitespace-delimited Russian words; qm-question-articles/v1, correct lmi target ref, empty question_refs, 3 HTTPS links and draft status. I opened IAU's constellation table; ESA/Hubble 'Galaxy in a spin' https://esahubble.org/images/potw1242a/ (NGC 3344 in Leo Minor, face-on view, outer/inner rings, subtle bar, young central stars and edge star formation); and ESA/Hubble 'A Lonely Beauty' https://esahubble.org/news/heic1803/ (Leo Minor, foreground Milky Way stars at left, near-UV/optical/near-IR composite). Claims and self-check accurately distinguish projection from physical association.

ACCEPT. Canonical SHA-256: cd603b8d46e612ef563d53096bc83deb33bc39831830d51f149fb978d3a13f63. 184 words; correct lyn target ref, empty question_refs, 4 HTTPS links and draft status. I opened ESA/Hubble https://esahubble.org/images/potw1908a/ (NGC 2419 in Lynx, ~300,000 ly, Milky-Way orbit, two red-giant populations with helium/nitrogen differences) and NASA Caldwell 25 https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/science/explore-the-night-sky/hubble-caldwell-catalog/caldwell-25/ (identity, Lynx, distance, faint unresolved amateur view). Original research https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.02178 supports four analysed populations: 1G plus three helium-enhanced 2G groups, including extreme 2GC enrichment. The wording keeps the older two-group observation distinct from the later four-population analysis.

ACCEPT. Canonical SHA-256: fb723caf5480987dd407841919926a11db487858838f5c4b35936e13e29cc56e. 190 words; correct lup target ref, empty question_refs, 3 HTTPS links and draft status. I opened ESO 2013 https://www.hq.eso.org/public/news/eso1308/ (SN 1006 expanding ring in Lupus; VLT/VIMOS shock-front mapping; fast suprathermal protons are not cosmic rays themselves but may seed them) and NASA Hubble https://science.nasa.gov/asset/hubble/sn-1006-supernova-remnant-hubble/ (Lupus, 6,850 ly, event around 1 May 1006 and white-dwarf explosion). The article's historical/date qualifiers and caution about precursor protons are sound.

REVISE. Canonical SHA-256: 02b9bb5db3d44c8c79c5c8838d57f04a92f678915be4b38be837736604437d16. 194 words; structure and non-binary claims are otherwise sound (Musca association, ~1,800 ly, planetary-nebula explanation, ring projection and unresolved morphology). I opened NASA's 2012 release https://science.nasa.gov/asset/hubble/planetary-nebula-ngc-5189/ and ESO's 2010 item https://www.eso.org/public/ireland/images/potw1012a/; both are the dated origin of the 'unseen companion' speculation. But original later RV research https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.03373 reports discovery of a close binary nucleus, P_orb=4.04±0.1 days, with companion type only described as most plausibly a massive white dwarf. Replace the present-tense 'невидимый близкий спутник' hypothesis and update the corresponding NASA/ESO supports metadata to date it historically; add the 2015 original source. Safe replacement idea: 'Спектроскопическое исследование 2015 года выявило близкую двойную центральную звезду с периодом 4,04±0,1 суток; точный тип спутника и его роль в форме туманности остаются предметом исследования.' The self-check may retain that causation of the S shape is not established. I also opened later TESS records: 2020 arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09991 discusses photometric variability, while A&A 2020/2024 endpoints returned 403; no unverified inference from those inaccessible texts is needed for this correction.
